thread: Follow the passage of time from a shadow on a sundial to the moving parts of a clock, then into a watch small enough to carry. The swarm meets gnomons and hour lines, pendulums and escapements, and tiny mechanisms made to keep their own rhythm.

candidates.name: The British Sundial Society
candidates.why: Sundial designs, equations, and a register of fixed and mass dials offer shadow-casting gnomons, tilted faces, and curious hour lines.

candidates.name: National Technical Museum, Prague
candidates.why: Its timekeeping collection spans water clocks, sand timers, mechanical clocks, and models of clock escapements, giving the swarm an assortment of ways to measure a moment.

candidates.name: Musée international d'horlogerie
candidates.why: Watches, clocks, watchmaking tools, machines, and automata invite the swarm inside intricate portable mechanisms.

candidates.name: Museum of Timekeeping
candidates.why: Its collections and exhibitions bring together speaking clocks, watches, clocking-in machines, and horological tools.

candidates.name: Antiquarian Horological Society
candidates.why: Its articles and specialist groups explore wristwatches, electrical timekeeping, and the large mechanisms of turret clocks.

candidates.name: National Association of Watch & Clock Collectors
candidates.why: The museum's galleries introduce pocket watches, public clocks, Asian timekeepers, and the tools and skills of clockmaking.

candidates.name: History of Science Museum, Oxford
candidates.why: Portable sundials, early pendulum clocks, and other scientific instruments make timekeeping into a cabinet of ingenious shapes.

candidates.name: The Worshipful Company of Clockmakers
candidates.why: Its museum and archive contain watches, clocks, marine chronometers, sundials, and tools connected to the craft of making timekeepers.
